title: Oxocrebanine from Stephania pierrei exerts macrophage anti-inflammatory effects by downregulating the NF-kappaB, MAPK, and PI3K/Akt signalling pathways.
authors: Chulrik, Wanatsanan; Jansakun, Chutima; Chaichompoo, Waraluck; Tedasen, Aman; Yotmanee, Pathumwadee; Sattayakhom, Apsorn; Chunglok, Wilanee; Suksamrarn, Apichart; Chunglok, Warangkana
one_liner_zh: 该文研究植物化合物oxocrebanine的抗炎机制，仅含分子对接但对象为蛋白-小分子，非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无AI或MD方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Plant-derived medicinal compounds are increasingly being used to treat acute and chronic inflammatory diseases, which are generally caused by aberrant inflammatory responses. Stephania pierrei Diels, also known as Sabu-lueat in Thai, is a traditional medicinal plant that is used as a remedy for several inflammatory disorders. Since aporphine alkaloids isolated from S. pierrei tubers exhibit diverse pharmacological characteristics, we aimed to determine the anti-inflammatory effects of crude extracts and alkaloids isolated from S. pierrei tubers against lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-activated RAW264.7 macrophages. Notably, the n-hexane extract strongly suppressed nitric oxide (NO) while exhibiting reduced cytotoxicity. Among the five alkaloids isolated from the n-hexane extract, the aporphine alkaloid oxocrebanine exerted considerable anti-inflammatory effects by inhibiting NO secretion. Oxocrebanine also significantly suppressed prostaglandin E(2), tumour necrosis factor-alpha, interleukin (IL)-1beta, IL-6, inducible nitric oxide synthase, and cyclooxygenase (COX)-2 protein expression by inactivating the nuclear factor kappaB, c-Jun NH(2)-terminal kinase, extracellular signal-regulated kinase 1/2, and phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase/Akt inflammatory signalling pathways. Molecular docking analysis further revealed that oxocrebanine has a higher affinity for toll-like receptor 4/myeloid differentiation primary response 88 signalling targets and the COX-2 protein than native ligands. Thus, our findings highlight the potential anti-inflammatory effects of oxocrebanine and suggest that certain alkaloids of S. pierrei could be used to treat inflammatory diseases.
abstract_zh: 植物来源的药用化合物越来越多地被用于治疗急性和慢性炎症性疾病，这些疾病通常由异常炎症反应引起。Stephania pierrei Diels，在泰语中又称Sabu-lueat，是一种传统药用植物，用于治疗多种炎症性疾病。由于从S. pierrei块茎中分离出的阿朴啡类生物碱 (aporphine alkaloids) 展现出多样的药理特性，我们旨在测定S. pierrei块茎粗提物及分离出的生物碱对脂多糖 (lipopolysaccharide, LPS) 激活的RAW264.7巨噬细胞的抗炎作用。值得注意的是，正己烷提取物强烈抑制一氧化氮 (nitric oxide, NO)，同时表现出较低的细胞毒性。在从正己烷提取物中分离出的五种生物碱中，阿朴啡类生物碱oxocrebanine通过抑制NO分泌发挥了显著的抗炎作用。Oxocrebanine还通过失活核因子κB (nuclear factor kappaB)、c-Jun NH(2)-末端激酶、细胞外信号调节激酶1/2和磷脂酰肌醇3-激酶/Akt炎症信号通路，显著抑制了前列腺素E(2)、肿瘤坏死因子-α、白细胞介素 (interleukin, IL)-1β、IL-6、诱导型一氧化氮合酶和环氧合酶 (cyclooxygenase, COX)-2蛋白表达。分子对接分析进一步揭示，oxocrebanine对toll样受体4/髓样分化初级反应88信号靶点和COX-2蛋白的亲和力高于天然配体。因此，我们的发现强调了oxocrebanine的潜在抗炎作用，并提示S. pierrei的某些生物碱可用于治疗炎症性疾病。
